Bulletin #6 
February 22, 1968 


WE'RE OFF AND RUNNING 


- If our lst official report luncheon held yesterday is any incication of the future 
success of our overall campaign - then all we can say - is we have a winner on our 
hands this:-year. 


~ While all divisions are not fully underway,(they will be by this weekend) - we were 
still able to report the most successful lst report luncheon in our campaign history. 


1968 - $96,586 or 28.4% on our $30,000 objective. 
1967 - 62,595 or 19.4% on our $320,000 objective. 


- Lorne Main, who filled in for John McGiffin, was all smiles (but, again, have you 
ever seen Lorne when he wasn't smiling?) 


HIGHLIGHTS OF 1ST REPORT LUNCHTON 


1. John Saunders, Headmaster, Sir George Williams Evening Flementary & Hich School 
opened the eyes of most of us - he told us about the vital job the evening school 
is performing for Montreal people: 

Some statistical facts:- 

- 3500 Evening Stucents enrolled during current year. 

- Average age of last year's eraduates 2).6 years. 

- Students represent over 28 countries of the world. 

- One fifth at least of student body is French Canadian. 
All of us working on the campaign organization are proud to realize that half of 
our yearly grant t Sir George Williams is used by the Elementary and High School 
Department.

3. A BIG JOB AHEAD - Paul Zimmerman and Paul Cote of the Special Names Division 
have been putting forth tremendous effort - re assessing card potential and 
broadening the base of supnort. "New Money is the Key" said Paul at our meeting, 
"If we wait until mic March before we search out new sunport - it will be too 
late". Special Names requires 26,000 in new money in order to reach its objective.
